description: A policy update that grants nothing the old policy did not grant does not introduce least-privilege issues, whatever its statement ids.

cases.name: narrowing a policy under a new Sid is not a new least-privilege issue (source case: forms-deploy 951687f6b, s3:* on arn:aws:s3:::* narrowed to s3:PutObject on objects)
narrowing with a condition under new Sids is not a new issue (source case: terraform-aws-eks 60dcc4506)
guard: a new action outside the old grants is a new issue
guard: dropping a condition widens the policy, so its issues are new
guard: removing a Deny widens the policy, so its issues are new
review: a statement whose Effect is not known statically is never taken as a Deny or as covered
review: turning a Deny into an Effect not known statically is not a kept Deny
review 4: a change of policy language version is never taken as granting nothing new
review 5: an inline policy that moves to another role grants that role something new, however narrow
review 5: an inline policy narrowed for the same role (by reference) is not a new issue
review 10: a statement without a Resource is never covered
review 11: an IAM policy variable in a new grant can be anything, so it is not covered by an old pattern
review 17: an inline policy whose role is replaced in the same change belongs to a new principal
review 18: an inline policy naming its role by a known attribute of a replaced role belongs to a new principal
review 19: a condition on a value not known statically never proves the grant unchanged
an inline policy naming its role by a literal name belongs to a new principal when that role is replaced in the same change
an inline policy naming its user by a literal name belongs to a new principal when a user of that name is deleted and created in the same change
guard: an inline policy naming its role by a literal name keeps the same principal when another role is replaced
review 21: a narrowed inline policy whose remaining issues read the same is new when its user is deleted and created in the same change
review 21: a principal whose name is sensitive is matched by the name it holds
review 22: an inline policy of a new principal keeps its full result: a retained FAIL is not hidden behind a new WARN
principal identity: an owner name is compared without case, so "App" names a role "app" replaced in the same change
principal identity: an owner name that only changes case keeps the same principal
principal identity: a user renamed in place keeps its inline policy when the policy names it by .name
principal identity: a user renamed in place keeps its inline policy when the policy names it by .id
principal identity: a group renamed in place keeps its inline policy when the policy names it by .name
principal identity guard: a policy that moves to another user renamed in place is new to that user
principal identity: an owner named through a reference to a user this change keeps is that user, not any new user of unknown name
principal identity guard: an owner named literally is still matched against a new user of unknown name
